findings.title: Power-integral estimates discard logarithmic and bounded regimes used in the core envelope proof
findings.verification: N=4,delta=1/3 gives integral_a^R dt/t=log(R/a), while (3.6) asserts an R-independent bound. On a<t<R, |yprime|<t^(2/3), |y|<=sqrt(2)t and section volume |B_3|t^2, so the actual T_delta moment has a positive logarithmic lower bound. Multiplication by |x|=R produces R log R. For N=4,delta=1/4 the corresponding positive integral tends to a nonzero constant while the printed power tends to zero.
findings.assumption_check: delta=1/3 and 1/4 are both permitted, N=4 is in scope, lower cutoff fixed, R can tend to infinity. T_delta is the explicit auxiliary majorant, not asserted to be a true coincidence set.
findings.counterevidence: A complete repair is proved: choose delta=1/4, retain the constant first moment and linear term, and compare integrands before integration. This restores V_C>=-C(1+|x|) and the paraboloid envelope. The main classification is not disproved.
findings.severity_reason: False estimate is explicitly used in the proof of the envelope needed by the core matching/ordering argument; repairability does not remove that dependency.
findings.version_limit: The distinct author-hosted copy retains the displayed estimate chain, with delta<=1/3; this is selective comparison only, no VoR attribution.

findings.title: Unnormalized uniqueness of the ellipsoid with prescribed quadratic blow-down
findings.verification: Dilation gammaP corresponds to Eprime->sqrt(gamma)Eprime and preserves p via gamma^2*u(x/gamma). The radial Newtonian potential of every ball of radius a has interior difference -r^2/(2d), independent of a. An independently derived explicit family in R3 with contact rho^2<=2*s*z has the same blow-down rho^2/4 for all s>0, with exact PDE and boundary verification.
findings.counterevidence: The core construction requires existence of one choice and deliberately varies gamma; absolute uniqueness is unnecessary. Add a scale normalization or remove the uniqueness word.
findings.severity_reason: False extra uniqueness has no demonstrated essential downstream use.
findings.version_limit: Same uniqueness wording observed in distinct author-hosted copy; no VoR claim.

findings.title: General blow-down lemma omits the zero solution
findings.verification: u identically zero is smooth, nonnegative, solves Delta u=indicator(u>0), and all quadratic rescalings are zero. Zero is neither a half-space solution nor a trace-one quadratic form.
findings.counterevidence: Definition 2.8 excludes the zero solution both geometrically and through its prescribed blow-down. Theorem 1.1 may be read with an implicit nontriviality or degenerate-cylinder convention; that convention should be explicit. No new nontrivial class is shown.
findings.severity_reason: Degenerate case is excluded in the actual monotone proof and does not damage its core conclusion.
findings.remedy: Add u not identically zero to Lemma 2.3 or include a zero alternative; make theorem convention explicit.

local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.observation: G(t0)/t0^(2delta) has coefficient (1-2delta) log t0, not (2-2delta).
local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.check: For delta<1/2 it still dominates the t0^delta bound for sufficiently large t0; compare functions h and G exactly.
local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.impact: Arithmetic slip without failure of the needed existence estimate.

local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.observation: At gamma_infty=0 the text specifies u_infty=p. Its contact set is the full vertical axis, rather than a literal zero dilation or positive half-axis.
local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.check: The full axis also has locally zero 2-capacity, via logarithmic transverse cutoffs.

local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.observation: The sign of b3 can be tested at -e3/2 within the stated ball of convergence.
local_clarifications_not_additional_scie.impact: No need to assert convergence on an exterior ball.

combined_assessment: No counterexample to the nontrivial classification theorem is established; do not attribute these findings to the journal final.

checks.independent_reasoning: Read source lines 908-923 and 1045-1073. At N=4, delta=1/3, section exponent is 2, so the first-moment integrand is t^-1 and the claimed power is zero. Restricting a<t<R and |yprime|<t^(2/3) proves the actual geometric integral has a positive logarithmic lower bound; this is not merely a defective majorant. The lower cutoff is fixed. Multiplication by R makes the printed envelope derivation fail. Delta=1/4 is permitted by Lemma 2.10; then first moment exponent -9/8 is integrable at infinity, potential/tail exponents <=7/8, and retaining the linear term gives the claimed repair. No coincidence-set counterexample or false classification theorem is inferred.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: The repaired proof shows a local repair suffices, but Proposition 4.1 is explicitly used in the core expansion/matching chain (source lines 1439,1458,1462,1955). Under the assigned standard the invalid core derivation remains Major.

checks.independent_reasoning: Read Lemma 6.1 statement and Step 1, source 1672-1720. The source asserts unique Eprime while allowing every gamma>0. Rescaling u_gamma(x)=gamma^2 u(x/gamma) preserves the degree-two blow-down, and gamma P_E=P_(sqrt(gamma)E). The radial potential difference -r^2/(2d) is independent of radius. Reconstructed the explicit parabolic-coordinate check: (xi*gprime)prime+h=xi/4 and (xi*hprime)prime=1/4, yielding Delta u=1; all value/first derivatives vanish at xi=s. Thus the example satisfies the claimed PDE and boundary matching.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: The subsequent construction needs one Eprime and later varies scale explicitly; no essential use of absolute uniqueness is demonstrated. Minor is appropriate.

checks.assessment: confirmed literal scope defect; Minor retained
checks.independent_reasoning: Read equation (1.1), Lemma 2.3 lines 499-518, and Definition 2.8 lines 577-586. u=0 satisfies the unqualified PDE, but its rescalings do not have a unit-direction half-space or trace-one quadratic limit. No nontriviality assumption appears in this lemma. Definition 2.8 excludes it both by the contact-set half-space/boundary condition and by positive-definite trace-one transverse blow-down.
